candidates.title: cartesi.hash-tree frontier_forest_expand_leaf rejects a valid expansion after frontier_forest_store/load: 'leaf height mismatch'. The file for a fixed-point subtree keyed by hash can be rewritten with an equal-hash tree of a lower base height
candidates.component: Lua helper library cartesi.hash-tree (frontier_forest_* functions), used by the PRT player's computation-hash trees
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md table: 'the frontier and forest functions of cartesi.hash-tree'). It stands in for the honest operator's computation-hash proof producer only where prt.lua reaches the defect, and prt.lua does not reach it (see reachability)
candidates.location: src/cartesi/hash-tree.lua: frontier_forest_expand_leaf (fixed-point branch: 'container, key, container_height = values, ..., tree.base_height', then 'assert(is_tree(tree) and container_height > height, "leaf height mismatch")' ~line 1031); store_tree (~702-718), which rewrites the file named by tree.hash with the encoding of whichever equal-hash tree is stored last; load_tree (~552-583)
candidates.description: Forest files are keyed by hash only. Two fixed-point trees can have the same hash and height but different base heights, for example base 0 over [a,b,a,b] and base 1 over [H(a,b)] (padded). The one stored last owns the file. After frontier_forest_load, every occurrence of that hash loads the file's representation. Suppose that representation has a base height below the height of the expansion that was valid in memory. frontier_forest_expand_leaf then jumps straight to the fixed-point tree's base values, lands below the requested height, and fails its assertion. The same call on the same forest before the store succeeds, and node queries on the reloaded forest still work. So a store/load round trip changes the result of a documented operation ('Expands a subtree of a full forest using a full forest of the same height and root hash ... Stored trees on the path load as in a query').
candidates.trigger: A caller of the library builds a forest that holds equal-hash subtrees with different fixed-point base heights, stores and reloads it, then calls frontier_forest_expand_leaf at the coarser base height. Minimal case: append {a,b,a,b} at height 0, then pad_back H(a,b) twice at height 1 (or the reverse order), store, load, expand position 0 at height 1 with a forest over {a,b}.
candidates.reachability: Not reached on the honest path as far as I can tell. prt.lua calls frontier_forest_expand_leaf (open_bundle) only after frontier_forest_get_node_hash or get_siblings returns nil, that is, when the path is opaque. In the failing case the reloaded representation is finer, so the query succeeds and no expansion is attempted. The PRT forests also push values only at bundle height or above (mcycle: LOG2_BUNDLE_MCYCLE_COUNT=4; uarch: bundle height 20 = one bundle per mcycle). The only base-0 fixed-point trees are whole bundles of height exactly the bundle height, so an equal-hash tree with a base below the expansion height should not arise there. Reaching it needs a caller that uses the API outside the player's pattern.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies outright. The trigger is a sequence of documented library calls, not a snapshot the emulator did not write. 2 Role: Support ('the Lua helper libraries (... the frontier and forest functions of cartesi.hash-tree ...)'). Section 3: 'A library stands in for the most critical role among the components that reach the defect through it.' The PRT player (itself support) does not reach it per the reachability argument. 3 High/Medium: Medium for support needs 'when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. No honest-operator path shows it, so it does not qualify. If a reviewer finds a prt.lua path that expands a non-opaque fixed-point node after a reload, it would rate Medium (support standing in for the honest operator: R4 'produce every requested node and proof', R2 'Every way of copying, persisting, restoring ... must agree'). 4 Critical: no, it is not on the honest operator's path. 5 Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model' -> Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None as reached today. It is a latent persistence-dependent failure in the library that computation-hash proofs depend on. A future caller that expands unconditionally after a restart (the player reloads forests from disk on relaunch) would fail to produce a proof that it could produce before the restart.
candidates.evidence: Randomized differential fuzz (forest-fuzz.lua: 4 seeds x 150 trials, heights 1-9, push_back/append/pad_back/subforest values/raw subforest roots/expand_leaf/store/load). It found 0 mismatches against a naive node map for node hashes, siblings and verify_slice, before and after expansion and after a store/load round trip. In 'preload' mode (store and load, then expand) it gives repeated 'expand failed ... leaf height mismatch'. Minimal deterministic reproduction expand-min.lua: order 2 (pad_back first, then append) gives 'in-memory: expand true', 'reloaded: node true, expand false .../hash-tree.lua:1031: leaf height mismatch'. Files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r4/RGPROOF/expand-min.lua, forest-fuzz.lua
candidates.test_idea: Build the minimal forest in both orders, store and load it, and assert that frontier_forest_expand_leaf(g, 0, sub) succeeds on the reloaded forest exactly as on the in-memory one, followed by equal get_node_hash/get_siblings. Exit 1 while the reloaded call raises 'leaf height mismatch'.

not_covered: No on-chain (EVM) check of machine-state proofs produced by get_proof: LibMachineValidityProof/OutputValidityProof in cartesi-rollups-contracts were not run against the emulator's proofs. I only relied on earlier rounds' constant checks.
prt-ethereum.lua encoders (claim, validity_proof, append_log) were read, not fuzzed or run through Dave on the chain harness.
get_proof/get_node_hash on machines loaded with sharing (SHARING_CONFIG/ALL), on clone_stored copies, after replace_memory_range, and with the page-hash-tree cache restored from a stored phtc file.

Proofs after host faults (exceptions inside hash_tree::update or log producers). Those belong to R3-VARDIRTY-1/2. A leftover borrowed page-cache entry makes get_page_proof's 'assert(opt_br)' a release-build null dereference; this was reasoned about only.
The hash-tree concurrency runtime option (parallel update) combined with get_proof: all runs used the defaults.

Linux templates (valid-template, valid-template-calc): sweeps ran only on the bare-metal template, on custom configs with non-power-of-two RAM and flash drives (up to 0x007fffffc0000000), on SHA-256 machines (create/run/write only; the uarch refuses SHA-256), via JSON-RPC including fork_server, and after store, load and clear_hash_tree.
verify_hash_tree strength: it returns true without checking dense or sparse inner nodes and only prints an ar-node/dense-root mismatch. Already noted by R3-VARDIRTY. Not evaluated further.

Worst-case get_proof cost was not measured reliably: the host load average was about 18 on 4 CPUs. Each get_proof costs a few ms because update_hash_tree rehashes the always-dirty pages, which is bounded.
The CLI --initial-proof/--final-proof at a rejected yield (a possible variant of R3-VARSPEC-4) and cartesi-machine-stored-hash.lua.
Record-step (main-processor) proofs, which are ZK-only; JSON-RPC client parsing of hash_tree_proof sibling arrays (known; trusted server).
End-to-end computation-hash proofs from the PRT player (tree:get_proof with bundle opening) against Dave on the chain.
